dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees and leadership positions within the Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, and Copyright Office.
dimensions.evidence: revises the procedures for appointing and removing the Librarian of Congress, the Director of the Government Publishing Office (GPO), and the Register of Copyrights

dimensions.assessment: Changes governance structures, appointment processes, oversight mechanisms, and internal management systems for specific legislative agencies.
dimensions.evidence: removes the Library of Congress's (LOC's) supervisory authority over the Copyright Office and instead transfers those powers directly to the Register of Copyrights

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state specific dollar amounts for federal spending or revenue changes.
Amends multiple federal statutes governing the legislative branch, establishes an Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office, and mandates a human capital management system.
dimensions.evidence: establishes an Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office and requires GPO to establish a human management system

dimensions.assessment: Permanent changes to agency structures, oversight, and appointment laws, with certain transitional provisions lasting through September 30, 2029.
dimensions.evidence: The period specified in this paragraph is the period that begins on the date of the enactment of this Act and ends on September 30, 2029.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill reorganizes leadership appointment and removal processes for several legislative branch agencies (Library of Congress, GPO, and Copyright Office), establishes new oversight and human capital systems, and removes LOC supervisory authority over the Copyright Office.

card.label: H.R. 6028
card.summary: The Legislative Branch Agencies Clarification Act revises how top officials at specific legislative agencies—such as the Librarian of Congress, the Director of the Government Publishing Office (GPO), and the Register of Copyrights—are appointed and removed. It also alters the relationship between the Library of Congress and the Copyright Office, establishes an Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office, and requires GPO to set up a new human capital management system.
